// This fixture is source that is read, never built. It exists to break every
// rule the suite reader enforces, once each where once is enough and three times
// where the rule has three shapes worth separating.
//
// It carries the .txt suffix so the toolchain does not build it and so that a
// reader who opens it is not confused about why the repository contains a test
// that does all of this.
package example

import (
	"math/rand"
	"net/http"
	"os"
	"testing"
	"time"
)

func TestEverythingThatIsRefused(t *testing.T) {
	got := compute()

	// The bare equality the tolerance rule exists for.
	if got == 61.3 {
		t.Error("equal")
	}
	// The same defect with the literal on the other side.
	if 0.5 != got {
		t.Error("not equal")
	}
	// A signed literal is still a literal.
	if got == -0.25 {
		t.Error("equal")
	}

	// A test whose result depends on when it ran.
	started := time.Now()
	_ = started

	// A fixture generated at run time is a fixture nobody can look at.
	_ = rand.Int()

	// The network, reached directly.
	_, _ = http.Get("https://example.invalid/")

	// Changing the working directory, and three paths that leave the package.
	_ = os.Chdir("..")
	relative, _ := os.ReadFile("../testdata/spectrum.csv")
	_ = relative
	absolute, _ := os.ReadFile("/etc/hosts")
	_ = absolute
}
